samples.summary: Web OAuth state comparison is never tested with two equal-length, different values — the actual byte comparison in `timingSafeEqualString` is unexercised in the failing direction
samples.evidence: The three rejection cases in the `it.each` at auth.controller.spec.ts:265-268 are: cookie 'mine' vs state 'theirs' (lengths 4 vs 6 — rejected by the `left.length === right.length` short-circuit alone), no cookie at all (rejected by `typeof cookie !== 'string'`), and no state (rejected by `!stateToken`). The only positive case ('web-state' vs 'web-state') exercises the equal branch. So if `timingSafeEqual` were dropped/inverted such that equal-length-but-different states compared as equal, every test in this file would still pass — and that is exactly the CSRF-binding bypass this code exists to prevent. No same-length mismatch case (e.g. cookie 'aaaaaaaa' vs state 'bbbbbbbb') appears anywhere in the file.
searchedFor: read cookies.ts and github-auth.guard.spec.ts for any state-compare test

samples.summary: The renamed `__cliStateToken` → `__oauthState` hand-off from guard to strategy has no test on the strategy side
samples.evidence: `GitHubAuthGuard` now sets `req.__oauthState` (guard spec asserts this at github-auth.guard.spec.ts:62,138) and `GitHubStrategy.authenticate` reads `(req as {__oauthState?: string}).__oauthState` to populate `opts.state` (github.strategy.ts:59-66). github.strategy.spec.ts contains only endpoint-configuration tests — nothing invokes `authenticate` or asserts that `opts.state` is forwarded. A property-name drift between the two files (the diff renames the property in both) would silently drop the `state` on every authorization request and no test in packages/backend would fail; only the callback's own check would surface it, at runtime.
searchedFor: glob packages/backend/src/auth/* for any other strategy spec

samples.summary: The nonce-less CLI redirect branch (`nonceParam === ''`) is not asserted anywhere; the existing CLI redirect assertion matches with or without a nonce
samples.evidence: auth.controller.ts:152-157 builds the loopback redirect with `&nonce=...` only when `cliState.nonce` is set. The only test covering a nonce-less CLI state (auth.controller.spec.ts:189-212) asserts `expect.stringMatching(/^http:\/\/127\.0\.0\.1:9876\/callback\?code=.+/)`, which matches a URL that also carries `&nonce=`, so it cannot detect the branch being wrong. The nonce-present test (line 226) only uses `stringContaining('&nonce=nonce-abc')`. Also untested: `encodeURIComponent` on the nonce (no nonce value in any test needs encoding), and `CliAuthStore` nonce round-trip in cli-auth.store.spec.ts, whose `consumeState` test at line 35 still asserts `{csrf, mode, port}` (passes either way under `toEqual` because `nonce` is `undefined`).
searchedFor: read the CLI-flow describe block of auth.controller.spec.ts

samples.summary: `registerLoginCommand`'s action wiring is untested: the `--allow-unbound-callback` flag→option mapping and the classify/print/exit handler are never driven through commander
samples.evidence: packages/cli/test/login.test.ts drives `runLogin(options, deps)`, `startCallbackServer`, `fetchLoginSession`, `nonceMatches` and `classifyLoginFailure` directly. Nothing parses `['login', '--allow-unbound-callback']` through a commander program, so the wire from the declared flag name (login.ts:70-73) to `LoginOptions.allowUnboundCallback` (read at login.ts:227,234) is asserted only against a hand-written options object — a rename of either side would leave the downgrade flag silently inert with all tests green. The `.action` catch block (login.ts:79-87: classify → `console.error(message)` → `process.exit(code)`) likewise has no test.
searchedFor: read packages/cli/test/login.test.ts (as added in the diff)

samples.summary: Two new image-fetcher branches have no test: the `INVALID_PROXY` SystemError and the `data:` path through `createImageFetcher`
samples.evidence: `hopDispatcher` (image-fetcher.ts:479-497) raises `SystemError('INVALID_PROXY', ...)` when `new ProxyAgent(proxy)` throws for a malformed `http_proxy`; packages/cli/test/image-fetcher.test.ts stubs only well-formed proxies (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, `http://127.0.0.1:1`) and never asserts INVALID_PROXY. Separately, `assertFetchableImageUrl` returning `null` for `data:` is unit-tested, but no test drives `createImageFetcher(...)('data:image/png;base64,...')` end to end, so the null-dispatcher path through `fetchOrThrow`/`res.blob()` is uncovered. Also uncovered: bracketed IPv6 entries in `no_proxy` (`splitHostPort`'s bracketed branch) — the `proxyForUrl` suite tests only name/suffix/port/`*` forms.
searchedFor: read the full proxy and SSRF-gate describe blocks in packages/cli/test/image-fetcher.test.ts
